Depending on whether you are looking at real-world physics, aerospace engineering, or science fiction tropes, "repulsion field thrusters but reverse" translates to a few distinct concepts: 
1. The Real Physics Equivalent: Attractor / Tractor Fields
If a repulsion field uses magnetic or electrostatic forces to push an object away, its direct reverse is an attractor field or electrostatic/electromagnetic docking system. 
  • How it works: Instead of utilizing like charges or aligned magnetic poles to push away, the system switches polarity to create a localized attractive force (like a tractor beam). 
  • Real-world use: This concept is actively utilized in space docking mechanisms and Magnetoplasmadynamic (MPD) thrusters, which use internal Lorentz forces to pinch, pull, and accelerate plasma to extreme velocities. 
2. The Aerospace Equivalent: Thrust Reversers
If you mean a thruster that physically acts in the opposite direction to slow a vehicle down rather than push it forward, it is called a thrust reverser. 
  • How it works: In commercial aviation, engines use mechanical blocker doors or cascading vanes to redirect the backward rush of air forward and outward.
  • The Result: It creates a massive aerodynamic braking force, allowing heavy aircraft to decelerate rapidly upon landing. 
3. The Plasma Physics Twist: Field-Reversed Configuration (FRC)
If you are looking at cutting-edge electric propulsion, there is a literal "reverse field" technology known as a Rotating Magnetic Field (RMF) Thruster. 
  • How it works: It uses an induced current to completely reverse a steady axial magnetic field.
  • The Result: This field reversal traps a high-density pocket of plasma (a "plasmoid") inside a magnetic cage. The thruster then shoots these magnetically isolated plasma pockets out the back at extreme speeds without eroding the engine itself. 
4. The Sci-Fi Equivalent: Gravity Wells / Singularity Drives
In science fiction, where "repulsion fields" are often shorthand for anti-gravity or shields, the reverse is an artificial gravity well generator or inertia dampener. Instead of pushing space-time away to propel a ship forward, it pinches space-time in front of the ship, effectively pulling the vessel forward into a localized gravitational dip.
